- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- When recent history shows strong downward momentum, model often fails to fully correct downward bias; apply mean reversion bias correction toward prior 7–14 day average.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ to 72+) are common; cap forecast peaks at +3–5% above recent high unless sentiment shifts strongly bullish.
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 10+ days, reduce forecast volatility and favor conservative mean-reversion paths.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating recent trends; especially when price has recently stabilized or reversed, model often over-anticipates continuation.
- When true outcome shows sharp reversal from high, model frequently fails to adjust downward quickly; apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day after peak if sentiment remains neutral.
